common-ground.line: A better question changes what comes next.
common-ground.heading: Before the first quote.
common-ground.detail: Field journal · Home energy · Research proposal
common-ground.quote: What makes the next step feel possible?
common-ground.support: A study of the space between wanting a warmer home and knowing where to start.
common-ground.demoTitle: Follow the evidence, not just the theme.
common-ground.demoIntro: These notes are synthetic examples, not participant findings. Explore how an observation might lead to a testable decision.

evidence.observation: S01 · Illustrative note: a household asks a neighbour for an installer name before opening a comparison site.
evidence.interpretation: Personal recommendations may reduce perceived risk. One example cannot establish how common this is.
evidence.action: Investigate how households verify recommendations; compare people who proceed with people who stop.

evidence.observation: S02 · Illustrative note: a renter saves upgrade information but cannot approve changes to the property.
evidence.interpretation: The person researching may not control the decision. Price comparison may be premature.
evidence.action: Recruit tenants and property decision-makers separately; map the consent and responsibility handoff.

evidence.observation: S03 · Illustrative note: a household abandons research after discovering that preparation work is needed first.
evidence.interpretation: The sequence of work may be less clear than the choice of product.
evidence.action: Test a readiness checklist against a quote-first entry point, including households with unfinished attempts.

waypoint.line: A direction teams can act on.
waypoint.heading: Fewer bets. Shared momentum.
waypoint.detail: Strategy memo · A proposed first 90 days
waypoint.support: Three teams. One customer journey. A clear reason for what comes first.
waypoint.demoIntro: Choose a first investment. The effort units and consequences are illustrative; they make a trade-off explicit rather than predict delivery.

bets.name: Shared identity
bets.why: Give customers one account across products before expanding the journey.
bets.tradeoff: Defer the visual refresh. Reserve two units for squad integration and two for support and learning.

bets.name: Connected setup
bets.why: Remove repeated setup, while accepting a dependency on the existing identity model.
bets.tradeoff: Defer shared identity work. Two units remain for integration; there is no separate refresh capacity.

bets.name: Visual refresh
bets.why: Improve visual consistency, while leaving repeated account and setup steps unresolved.
bets.tradeoff: Defer journey changes. Three units remain, but a coherent appearance does not resolve the customer friction.
